name: Ki-67 proliferation index
summary: Ki-67 is a nuclear proliferation antigen whose immunohistochemical index provides prognostic information in early hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, but analytical variability limits its use for individual treatment decisions.
biology: Ki-67 is expressed in all active phases of the cell cycle (G1, S, G2, M) and absent in quiescent (G0) cells, making it a marker of the growth fraction. Its suppression after short-term preoperative endocrine therapy reflects pharmacodynamic response and has been studied as a dynamic prognostic marker.
alterations: Low, intermediate and high proliferation index (cut-offs vary by guideline and laboratory)

methods: Immunohistochemistry (MIB-1 clone) with standardised scoring as recommended by the International Ki67 in Breast Cancer Working Group
testing.specimen: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumour tissue (core biopsy or resection)
testing.notes: Interlaboratory reproducibility is best at the extremes of the range; intermediate values are least reliable. Digital image analysis and standardised counting methods improve consistency.

predictiveRelevance: Ki-67 is mainly prognostic and helps distinguish luminal A-like from luminal B-like tumours. It has been used to define high-risk populations in some adjuvant trials, and on-treatment Ki-67 after short-term preoperative endocrine therapy can identify endocrine-resistant tumours. Genomic expression assays generally provide more reproducible risk stratification.
